lead.hed: Marines will test contractors' cargo drones in Alabama this winter for front-line resupply
lead.insight: The Marine Corps and Navy will hold a demonstration in Huntsville from Jan. 25 to Feb. 5, 2027, for the second increment of the Tactical Resupply Unmanned Aircraft System, Defense News reports. Monday's Navy announcement says the aircraft is meant to supply small units across the last tactical mile. One required flight carries 100 pounds up to 40 nautical miles, drops the load and returns without refueling. The other carries 150 pounds or more out to 10 nautical miles. The drones must reach at least 50 knots and launch and recover without a catapult, net or cable. The Marines also want them to assess landing zones and avoid people and terrain on their own. The announcement did not say what cargo the system will carry.

political.hed: Virginia polls close at 7 p.m., and anyone in line by then may still vote
political.insight: Voters are deciding a U.S. Senate race between Sen. Mark Warner, a Democrat, and Republican Bert Mizusawa, along with 11 House seats and three constitutional amendments, according to the Department of Elections. In the 7th District, which includes Fredericksburg, Democratic Rep. Eugene Vindman faces Republican Doug Ollivant, Libertarian Taner Demirci Lopez and independents Alaha Ahrar, Joshua Ertle and Randall Terry. The amendments cover abortion and other reproductive decisions, the state's ban on same-sex marriage, and automatic restoration of voting rights on release from incarceration.

political.hed: Former carrier Enterprise leaves Newport News on its last tow, bound for dismantling in Alabama
political.insight: The hulk of the nuclear aircraft carrier USS Enterprise left a Newport News Shipbuilding pier on Monday, almost 15 years after its final deployment, USNI News reports. The Navy awarded environmental contractor NorthStar $418 million for the disposal work, and shipbuilder HII dropped its legal challenge last month. The eight reactors make the job unusually hard: Nimitz and Ford-class carriers have two. USNI News reports the Navy has spent about $1.3 billion on the carrier's inactivation.

tech.hed: Binance traces its $6.3 billion theft to a fake job interview; North Korea denies any role
tech.insight: The exchange's post-mortem, released Tuesday, describes a campaign dating to June, The Record reports. In September, an engineer contacted about a job was told in a second interview to download an assignment holding malicious code. By Oct. 20 the attackers had reached two more devices, and by Oct. 29 they were inside critical wallet tools. Binance and other platforms froze about $2.85 billion. The FBI and other U.S. agencies blamed North Korea's TraderTraitor group over the weekend. Kim Yo Jong called the charge "absurd" on Monday.

tech.hed: Google and Japanese law enforcement take down a botnet hidden in 1.3 million Android TV boxes
tech.insight: The X.CPE botnet sat in set-top boxes across more than 200 countries, The Record reports. Google tied it to Videostrong, a Chinese device manufacturer, and accused the company of selling backdoor access to criminal affiliates. Videostrong did not respond to requests for comment. Google has banned the company from making devices with its preloaded apps and says cutting the control domains left the malware effectively benign. Google did not explain whether owners of infected devices will be notified.

tech.hed: Apple will require an 18+ rating on dating apps and AI companions with romantic or sexual content
tech.insight: Starting Nov. 16, developers must declare whether an app offers dating or relationship features, including a virtual companion that engages users in sexual or romantic content, Apple told developers on Monday. TechCrunch reports those apps will carry an 18+ rating and says the rule could affect AI companion apps such as Character.AI and Replika, which are often aimed at younger people. Developers must also declare whether an app shares a user's real-world location with another person or group. Every app must finish the declarations by Jan. 12, 2027.

culture.hed: Two massacres of Christians in one week drew little notice, an essay argues
culture.insight: Nine Christians were killed at a funeral procession at St. George's Orthodox Church in Jordan, and sixty were murdered in Ethiopia by gunmen who went house to house, the essay says. It faults major outlets for barely noting the religious motive. It draws on a new Aid to the Church in Need report, which finds about 220 million Christians directly exposed to persecution and harassment in 165 countries in 2023, up from 160 in 2021.

culture.hed: Will anyone sing our hymns in 2126? An essay asks what Christians are building to hand down
culture.insight: Cultural Christianity is making a comeback, the essay opens, and it hopes a focus on building a lasting culture comes with it. It argues that little from the present era is good enough to hand down to great-great-grandchildren, and asks which hymns, churches, art, furniture and books future generations of Christians will inherit.
